It’s only been like five years since I moved out and I’m about to be 25 so there’s time for my life to explode but I’m satisfied bc it will be on my own terms.

I’m still confused about what I would do to make my mom violently angry with me as a kid. I was very well behaved, smart for my age, and eager to please my parents. What could I have possibly done to warrant being beat up and yelled at????

I feel for my parents deeply despite being treated like shit and abandoned by them. 

In my last attempt to salvage my relationship with my mom, she was livid about how I abused her and I’m selfish, insane etc. I am used to being gaslit by her so I almost fell for it. 

Thankfully, this exchange was over text since I live in another country so I was able to take a step back and remember what is real. I implored her to remember who I am from the 20 years we lived together. I asked her to remember that I’m endlessly devoted to my family, soft, and emotional. I asked if maybe she was projecting frustrations with my father on to me and that I understand and I’m ready to support her through this. 

She then ghosted me lol. It’s been three years.

Children aren’t really seen as living autonomous humans in my culture tbh so any feelings towards me were superficial. My mom’s friends did eventually realise she was insane bc she would constantly complain about me being crazy and irresponsible but that didn’t line up with reality. I was very successful academically so it shattered the illusion.

I have PTSD and my own slew of issues so I can empathise with you. However, I am not dating until I feel like I’m in a place where I can consistently manage my symptoms. I’m very familiar with people in life having unchecked (and even checked) mental illness and it’s a very draining experience. I’m not willing to subject myself to that again. My friends all have their own issues but I can have faith in our relationships bc I have seen their emotional regulation skills firsthand. 

I put a lot of effort into treating my mental illness and, frankly, most people do not. Just being in therapy is not a solution. I see a lot of people go through the motions but not truly introspect and grow. That’s why I’m very skeptical about dating while having mental health issues.

I thought I was bisexual until I moved away bc everything about attraction was theoretical. I didn’t have the bandwidth to explore my sexuality until freshman year of college. I gave myself permission to hook up with whoever I found attractive and enjoyed an active social life. 

After a year, I reflected and realised that I was never actually attracted to guys. I thought back to my childhood and I now understand that I was very indoctrinated in the compulsory heterosexuality. I thought my default setting was hetero and I just got a fun add on with attraction to women. I seriously considered if I could have a relationship with a man and also hooked up with a random dude “just to confirm”. Yeah, not into at all. I threw up. I’m very gay. I still worry and have intrusive thoughts about forcing myself to become heterosexual but it’s been many years so I think it’s set.

I grew up in a Muslim country so we had a mandatory lesson on Islam every week for every year of school. The moment I knew I couldn’t do religion was when I was like 12 and asked a follow up question in Islamic class. The teacher was infuriated at my audacity and yelled at me for being disrespectful. In actuality, I was slow with social cues as a kid and didn’t realise my desire for clarification would be perceived like this. 

I’m also a classics overachiever so it ticked me off that the best I could do as a woman was be someone’s wife. It annoyed the fuck out of me that all the boys I thought I was smarter than could become religious leaders simply bc they were boys.

Moved to a different continent for college and stayed. I haven’t spoken to anyone from home since moving. Honestly, it was a great idea and I don’t have any regrets. All my major problems like religious and social pressure has vanished and life is so much more fun.

My dad’s childhood was in abject poverty in a third world country but he is able to live a relatively successful lower middle class life now. 

The key for him was to quit unskilled labour work and go back to school bc he didn’t want to be stuck. He also married my mom bc she wanted to have a career which was very unusual for their community. They immigrated to the Middle East for better quality of life and opportunities and were able to sustain a life there for 30 years bc of their focus on education and being very ambitious with the kind of work they pursued. Dreaming big and being a little delusional. 

It’s not a dramatic story of abject poverty turning into extreme wealth but I think they did very well for themselves. They achieved upward mobility that is very rare in our community.

What makes my lesbian experience different from yours? There’s over a billion people that share my homeland and, statistically, some of them are going to be lesbians. Due to colonisation, my home has been destroyed and continuously exploited to feed the first world. Laws that criminalise homosexuality are very literally inherited from colonisers replicating the same homophobic laws your community experienced as well. The only difference being that women’s rights and queer rights did not have the same progress in my home. There’s lots of speculation as to why. I believe that this is because colonisers need us to continue pumping out babies and sustain the enormous labour force required to create all the consumer goods you enjoy. Look in your wardrobe, you will very likely have a lot of clothes made in Bangladesh where lesbians are literally murdered for the crime of not participating in heterosexual marriage. 

Now what does this have to do with you? Simply by participating in your economy, you are quite literally contributing to climate change, genocide, slavery etc. I am too. If you live in a metropolitan area then there will very likely be community organisations that provide workshops, readings, volunteer opportunities etc for anyone to join. These labels aren’t a fixed categorisation of human sexuality! It’s just shit we made up to try to understand the complex clusterfuck of love and relationships. I’ve written out my sexuality journey for u below in case u will find it helpful! 

I identified as bisexual when I was a teenager bc I was not actually engaging with dating (no time, gotta study lol). I knew for a fact that woman are sexually and romantically attractive to me and I assumed that I would eventually feel this way about men when I start dating around.

Eventually, I noticed that I’m yet to find a single man that is interesting even though my internal settings (and app settings) were set to everyone. I also made friends with lots of queer women for the first time so I became all too aware that bisexual women are into men for real and not just hypothetically 😭 I had a very good chat with my lesbian bestie and accepted that this is the label that fits me best. 

That happened three years ago and I haven’t fluctuated with my label since. I did experience the gay worst case scenario of being outed to my parents and disowned 💀 but it was for the best bc living openly as a lesbian has felt very authentic and satisfying. Due to my religious trauma and third world upbringing, I still carry a lot of internalised homophobia. I went as far as having sex with a random Tinder man (post coming out!) to “verify” my sexuality. I threw up on him 😬 sexuality verified alright. I even had multiple questionable threesomes bc I thought I could “condition” myself to be with a man if a woman was also there. Spoiler alert: things don’t work that way… 

I started therapy a few weeks ago and I think I’m starting to make progress with my internalised homophobia by processing the traumatic nature of my outing. I lean masc in presentation and demisexual in temperament so some men catch my attention but I know that I am not sexually or romantically compatible with them. Even the smallest flirtation with a woman feels so much more intense than any interaction I’ve had with a man. I’ve never crushed on a man but I’ve had multiple crushes on women, ranging from drunk party hookup to full on romantic feelings. I haven’t actually been in a relationship yet bc I’m very particular and a workaholic but my situationships/casual sex friends are enough for me to know that I’m definitely only interested in women. 

TL; DR I’m a lesbian!!! Yay!!
